title: Causal Discovery through Synergizing Large Language Model and Data-Driven Reasoning

problem.claim: Causal discovery is hindered by insufficient high-quality data and by traditional causal discovery algorithms' limited ability to comprehend the exact semantics of variables.

gap.claim: Existing causal discovery approaches do not fully integrate metadata-based semantic reasoning with data-driven modeling, while LLM overconfidence and hallucination also require uncertainty analysis.

contributions.claim: Introduces LLM-CD, a causal modeling framework that integrates large language models' metadata-based reasoning with traditional causal discovery algorithms' data-driven modeling.

Deeply couples LLM reasoning with multiple stages of traditional causal discovery algorithms through an iterative process and quantifies LLM uncertainty using evidence-based deep learning theory and traditional algorithm assumptions.
Uses a new lung-cancer dataset extracted from MIMIC-IV alongside a hospital-provided de-identified patient dataset and two benchmark datasets for evaluation.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe LLM-CD as a novel causal modeling framework.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments across four datasets.
The authors report that LLM-CD is effective and reliable, with a highest Recall improvement of 403.93% and Ratio improvement of 25.77%.

narrative_sequence.summary: Causal mechanism discovery is important for scientific and technical progress.
Limited data quality and insufficient semantic understanding by traditional algorithms constrain causal discovery.
LLM-CD combines LLM metadata reasoning with traditional data-driven causal modeling, coupling them iteratively across algorithm stages.
The framework analyzes LLM uncertainty to address overconfidence and hallucination.
The authors evaluate the framework on four datasets and report improvements in Recall and Ratio.

source_observation.claim: The framework combines semantic metadata reasoning with data-driven causal modeling and iterative interaction.

interpretation.claim: Combining complementary reasoning modes may address limitations that either semantic reasoning or data-driven modeling faces alone.

application.claim: In another domain, pair domain-semantic reasoning with established data-driven methods and connect them through iterative refinement.

exception.claim: Such integration should account for uncertainty when the reasoning component is prone to overconfidence or hallucination.

source_observation.claim: The evaluation uses both real clinical data and benchmark datasets across four datasets.

interpretation.claim: Evaluation across heterogeneous datasets can provide evidence about performance beyond a single data source.

application.claim: Evaluate comparable methods across multiple real-world and benchmark datasets when assessing a data-driven framework.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that these datasets represent all deployment settings or that the reported gains generalize beyond the evaluated datasets.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the detailed architecture or implementation of LLM-CD.
The abstract does not identify the baselines, experimental protocols, statistical procedures, or uncertainty-analysis results.
The abstract does not provide absolute metric values or clarify how the percentage improvements were calculated.
